Prevention: Ensure that the fields are free of weeds which could harbour the insect
Uproot and burn crop residues at the end of the harvest as early as possible
Avoid leaving lots of trash in the field which might harbour the overwintering stages of the pest.
Avoid the application of broad spectrum pesticides in order to preserve natural enemies such as lady bird beetles and parasitic wasps and
Tachinid flies, which assist in reducing pest populations
Rotate cotton with alternate crops like cassava, or other vegetables every two years
Tasselling maize may act as trap crop because it is said to be more attractive to egg laying moth than cotton.
Monitoring: Eggs are cream, which turn brown and are laid individually.
Young larvae are yellowish- white to reddish-brown with prominent hairs.
Mature larvae are brown, green or pale yellow, with a characteristic dark band along the centre of the back.
A parallel pale band, a dark band and then another pale band traverse the sides of the body.
Spray the chemical when symptoms are first noticed or when there are 6 bollworms per 24 plants.
Direct Control: Hand pick all visible larvae and crush them.
Spray recommended insecticides indicated in the
Indoxacarb 400g/L (Steward 150EC) at the rate of 1ml/L of water.
Cypermethrin 200g/L (Cyrux 20EC; Cypermethrin 20EC) at the rate of 2.5-5mls/20L of water.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides
Pre-harvest interval (PHI) of 14 days; Re-entry interval (REI) 12 hrs.
Minimal interval between treatments is 5 days and make no more than 4 applications per crop.
